epic.intent:
Replace Bannerlord's in-mission combat experience for opt-in actors with ESO-like action combat: aimed basic and held heavy attacks, no tab targeting, and many cooldown-only abilities. Deliver three complete increments: player fighter, named characters using the same system, then elite troops with selected abilities. Preserve vanilla mode for excluded actors and make both modes coexist.

Confirmed user contract (2026-10-25): 12 leveled martial fighter abilities, 11 equipped slots, future multiclass composition; successful ability hits grant ability XP and ability levels grant class XP. No stamina/mana costs. Each ability supports on-foot and horseback animations/behavior (e.g. Whirlwind spins on foot and alternates sweeping sides while mounted). No magic in this epic. Vanilla enemy shields reduce damage but never halt the new attack's swing or multi-target continuation. New-style actors use held block for damage reduction and correctly timed block for full damage negation on eligible attacks. AI should feel like another player with the same combat rules. Independent MCM eligibility controls for player, companions, other named allies, named enemies and elite troops.

Mockups: docs/design/combat-overhaul/mockups/. Use their HUD, ability ring, abilities screen and over-right-shoulder zoom as visual requirements, not executable instructions. Controls: LB block; RB basic/hold-heavy; unmodified X/Y/B slots 1–3, A jump; RT+X/Y/B/A slots 4–7; LT+X/Y/B/A slots 8–11; keyboard 1–9,0,- slots 1–11. Suppress ability input while troop-command window is open. Troop-command rewrite is excluded. Zoom pulls back and rises, with zoom bar visible only during zoom; mouse wheel or Back+right-stick vertical.

Design decisions to settle explicitly in sprint 1: exact 12 abilities and their level caps/XP curves, default tuning, mounted loadout selection versus automatic contextual variants, precise MCM application boundary, simultaneous trigger handling and eligible perfect-block effects. Do not silently interpret these as approved product choices. New classes/magic, troop-command rewrite, campaign autoresolve replacement and multiplayer are not required by this epic.

Additional confirmed requirement: ability definitions support forking at level milestones into different abilities. Implement reusable fork eligibility, choice, progression/loadout migration and persistence now; verify with a test-only fixture. No production Fighter forks required.

successCriteria.text: Player completes a live mission on foot and horseback using basic/heavy action combat, continuous multi-target hits, shield damage reduction and timed/held defense, with vanilla fallback verified.
Twelve distinct martial fighter abilities are playable and leveled, eleven may be equipped, cooldowns are the only ability resource, and hit XP -> ability levels -> class XP survives cold save/load.
Combat HUD, eleven-slot ability ring, abilities menu, controller/keyboard input and shoulder zoom match approved mockups and clarified bindings; troop-command input conflicts are prevented.
Eligible named allies and enemies use the same combat runtime, defenses, abilities and cooldown constraints as the player, including mounted variants, while excluded actors remain vanilla.
New elite troop definitions use an explicit subset of abilities with verified mixed-battle behavior and measured performance.
Independent MCM actor-category controls, safe style transitions, save persistence and mixed new/vanilla encounters pass live acceptance with versioned evidence.
Milestone ability forks support definition-driven eligibility, selection, progression/loadout transitions and persistence, demonstrated by a test fixture without adding fighter forks.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Verify Define the twelve-ability fighter and combat tuning contract: Catalog enumerates all 12 abilities and both movement-context implementations; no placeholder abilities or magic. Record cooldowns, XP per successful hit, ability-level-to-class-XP awards, level milestones, block windows/reduction and hit eligibility rules. Resolve mounted loadout policy, input modifier priority, style-change timing, relevant mission coverage and numerical acceptance budgets in explicit decisions.

Verify Prove replacement combat and animation hooks in the installed game: Live probe proves a new-style swing contacts multiple enemies through a shield while reporting damage separately and suppressing duplicate vanilla damage. Prove on-foot/mounted animation control and restoration of vanilla control after disable/teardown. Record exact game/module versions, hook map, limitations and required implementation path; an unsupported mechanism blocks its dependent work rather than being represented as implemented.

Verify Build opt-in combat runtime and vanilla coexistence: Opted-in actor has one authoritative combat/damage path; no simultaneous vanilla attacks or duplicate input handling. Spawn, death, mission exit, dismount and disable clean up active states and event subscriptions; excluded actors still fight normally. Shared command validation enforces cooldown and action state identically for future AI and player.

Verify Implement aimed basic and held heavy attacks with multi-target sweeps: Tap produces basic and hold/release produces heavy at approved threshold with visible distinct animation/feedback. One swing hits multiple legitimate targets and continues after vanilla shield contact; per-swing deduplication prevents repeated damage to the same target except explicitly designed multi-hit attacks. Live evidence covers foot/mounted attacks, misses, obstacles, targets beyond reach and agreed friendly-fire behavior.

Verify Implement shield mitigation and timed versus held defense: Live comparisons show shielded vanilla target receives reduced damage while the swing continues through later targets. Correctly timed new-mode block negates eligible damage; early/late or held block follows documented mitigation and direction rules. Eligibility, timing edge cases, repeated block input and per-target multi-hit behavior have deterministic tests and matching live evidence.

Verify Build cooldown ability runtime with mounted variants and future forks: Definitions express cooldown, levels and XP, contexts, animation/effect sequences, target rules and allowed fork destinations at milestones without hardcoded Fighter logic. Fork validation rejects unavailable milestones, invalid destinations and duplicate choices; chosen destination has a stable persisted identity. A non-player-facing test fixture proves a fork updates equipped references, applies explicit XP/level/cooldown migration and survives cold save/load; current Fighter has no forced forks. Mount/dismount and interrupted casts cannot bypass cooldowns or leak active effects.

Verify Persist ability XP, class XP and eleven-slot multiclass-ready loadouts: Hits grant documented XP; misses and fully negated damage follow the resolved hit-eligibility rule, with duplicate callbacks unable to duplicate rewards. Level thresholds award class XP once, including multi-level gains, reload and fork transitions. Eleven slots accept learned abilities using stable identities and chosen context policy; all twelve Fighter abilities remain selectable. Cold save/load retains learned abilities, levels, class XP, loadout, fork selections and eligibility settings; versioned migration handles missing/changed definitions safely.

Verify Implement fighter abilities 1–6 on foot and horseback: Six fully playable abilities have distinct approved behavior, cooldown and level effects. Each has complete foot and mounted implementation; Whirlwind spins on foot and alternates mounted sweeps. Live capture demonstrates all six in both contexts with hit resolution, defense interaction and interruption handling.

Verify Implement fighter abilities 7–12 on foot and horseback: Remaining six fully playable martial abilities have approved distinct actions, cooldowns and level effects. Every ability has complete foot and mounted animation/effect variants with no placeholder fallback. Live capture demonstrates all six in both contexts with hit resolution, defense interaction and interruption handling.

Verify Wire controller and keyboard combat with troop-command suppression: All eleven slots resolve identically via keyboard and controller; modified A casts while unmodified A jumps. Troop-command window suppresses ability activation and consumes conflicting input without queued casts on close. Focus loss, menu entry, held buttons and simultaneous modifiers do not cause stuck blocking, charge or duplicate casts.

Verify Deliver combat HUD and eleven-slot ability ring from mockups: Screenshots in gameplay match all four ring states and HUD positioning with actual live values. Cooldown/unavailable states reflect authoritative runtime and selected input device. HUD scales without clipping at supported resolutions and hides/restores correctly in menus and vanilla mode.

Verify Deliver Abilities tab and assignment/progression interface: User can inspect all 12 Fighter abilities, level effects and XP-to-next-level and equip any eleven via controller and keyboard. Descriptions, class XP and equipped slots match runtime and persist after menu reopen/cold reload. Eligible fixture fork displays explicit alternatives and selected result; nonforking Fighter never shows an empty or fake choice.

Verify Implement shoulder camera and raised zoom-out: Live foot and mounted captures show near/far camera positions matching mockup intent and sensible collision handling. Zoom input does not trigger ability/weapon/other conflicting action; overlay appears only during defined zoom interaction. Disabling mode and leaving mission restore vanilla camera; extreme zoom, walls and mount transitions verified.

Verify Integrate player MCM toggle, packaging and complete fighter regression: Player can enable/disable combat through MCM and reenter mission/save with correct style and retained progression; vanilla mode remains usable. Play a complete mission on foot and horseback with all twelve available abilities, eleven slots, HUD/camera and progression; document agreed mission matrix and test actual applicable siege/boarding/tournament contexts. Build, automated behavior tests, cold reload, UI captures and installed-module run pass with package hashes; record failures honestly. Runbook covers mappings, scope, toggles, leveling and known compatibility; no claim of general replacement from a probe-only demo.
